adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:186 — No test covers assign() with an assignment_source pointing to a DIFFERENT integration than the target, so positive-sync coverage for the new cycle-prevention branch is incomplete

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds cycle-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` that returns `False` only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (issues.py). Tests cover `assignment_source=None` (outbound sync happens) and `assignment_source` matching the target integration (outbound sync prevented), but there is no test asserting that an `assignment_source` from a *different* integration still allows outbound sync, so the positive path for the new conditional branch isn’t fully covered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/tasks/test_sync_assignee_outbound.py — No test calls the sync_assignee_outbound celery task directly with a populated assignment_source_dict to verify AssignmentSource.from_dict parsing and pass-through into installation.sync_assignee_outbound; coverage only exists at the GroupAssignee.objects.assign level which mocks ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound and never exercises the dict-serialization/task layer

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an end-to-end path that *does* exercise the dict-serialization/task layer via GroupAssignee -> sync_group_assignee_outbound.apply_async -> tasks.sync_assignee_outbound parsing. In `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`, `GroupAssignee.objects.assign(..., assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))` causes `sync_group_assignee_outbound` to enqueue the celery task with `assignment_source_dict=assignment_source.to_dict()`. Under `with self.tasks():`, the task runs, calls `AssignmentSource.from_dict(...)`, and then `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`; the test’s `assert_not_called()` depends on successful parsing/matching of `integration_id` to block the outbound call. So it’s incorrect to say the dict/task layer is never exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/base.py:46 — sync_status_outbound signature change is present in the diff but no corresponding test changes appear to validate outbound status sync still works correctly after the signature change

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature in `src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py` by adding an optional `assignment_source` parameter, but the finding references `src/sentry/integrations/base.py:46`, which is not part of the provided diff. Also, the diff does not show any call-site or behavior changes for outbound status syncing—only assignee syncing gains new source/cycle-prevention logic and corresponding tests—so the claim that outbound status sync needs test updates is not directly supported by what’s shown here.
